title: Nine left
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Valentine's, a day late. The drugstore's card rack, red. Wood buys nothing. He has nine postcards of the bay left in the drawer. He counts them and puts them back.

panels.composition: The drugstore's card rack, the day after: red cards, half price, a sign as blocks. WOOD passing it without stopping. BARNABY.

image.prompt: a drugstore card rack of red valentine cards marked down, a young man passing without stopping, a small dog on a leash, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The postcard slot: restocked. The bay, faded blue. He doesn't take one.

image.prompt: close on a drugstore rack slot restocked with identical faded postcards of a bay, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The bedroom. The drawer. Nine postcards of the bay, counted onto the desk.

image.prompt: a young man counting nine identical postcards out of a desk drawer onto a desk, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Nine, back in the drawer. The drawer closed. The strip keeps the count: one used in December. Nine.

image.prompt: close on a desk drawer closing on a small stack of postcards, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: Nine left. The count of the drugstore's postcards continues.
